headline: Asia catches up with Wall Street's Huang rally as the Fed keeps a hike on the table

findings.headline: Asia is playing catch-up, led by the chip markets
findings.body: Korea and Taiwan, the purest read on AI chips, are rebounding hardest after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive and Wall Street's relief rally on Monday, with Japan and Australia following. Hong Kong and mainland China are muted because they trade on domestic policy and liquidity, not the Nvidia story. The scale of the Korean and Taiwanese moves shows how crowded the chip trade is in both directions.

sources.label: CNBC: Six key questions raised by Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
FT: What Nvidia tells us about America and China

findings.headline: The Fed did not join the relief
findings.body: New York Fed President Williams said there is still work to do on inflation and gave no pushback against the quarter-point December hike markets already price, not the softer tone Bessent and Ackman lobbied for at the weekend. Wednesday's October PCE inflation, the Q3 GDP revision and jobless claims, all landing before Thanksgiving, are now the main risk to the bounce, and thin holiday liquidity will exaggerate whatever they show.

sources.label: CNBC: Williams says higher rates likely 'over time'
New York Fed: Williams speech text

findings.headline: HPE shows AI good news is already paid for; Dell reports tonight
findings.body: Hewlett Packard Enterprise beat on its fiscal fourth quarter and raised its fiscal 2027 guidance, yet the shares fell after hours following a big jump in the session, on AI-server margin dilution and profit-taking. That sets a high bar for Dell and HP after today's US close, with Conference Board consumer confidence at 16:00 Zurich the other US test.

sources.label: Investing.com: HPE beats and raises, stock slips after big rally
MarketWatch via Morningstar: HPE's strongest growth ever, but its stock is sinking

view: Our view: Monday was a sentiment reset, not a change in the rate outlook. Asia's gains are a delayed echo of New York, and the test is whether they hold once the US reopens against a Fed still leaning hawkish ahead of Wednesday's PCE.
